why:
I checked every command in both briefs. Most of them are fine. `npm test` maps to `node --test`. The builder's `node -e "...Object.keys(m)..."` is valid, and verifier checks 1 and 2 are valid JS inside double quotes.

Verifier check 3 fails. Its script sits inside double quotes and builds `new RegExp('\\b'+n+'\\s*\\(')`. In bash double quotes, `\\` becomes `\`, so node receives `'\b'+n+'\s*\('`. In JS, `'\b'` is a backspace character, `'\s'` is just `s`, and `'\('` is just `(`. The pattern therefore becomes `<backspace>adds*(`. That pattern has an unterminated group, so `new RegExp` throws a SyntaxError on the first export. The check errors out whatever README.md contains, which means this command does not run as written.
